what: Which keys each sound actually answers to, as MIDI note numbers, inclusive.
why: The instrument does not publish this. There is no key-range field in seven-1.37.json, no opcode that reports one, and nothing in a recall burst that names a lowest or highest note. It is the one thing this app draws that cannot be read off the wire.
method: Played on the instrument and heard, and described in the player's own terms ("lowest A on the bed", "the top C") rather than as note numbers. tools/key-range.js will name keys as they are pressed if an exact figure is ever wanted. NOTHING here comes from the v1.22 manual — that manual is three firmware releases stale.
rules: A sound with no entry draws no keyboard. An absent range is not a full range — it is an unheard one, and a picture claiming a limit nobody has played is worse than no picture.
Ranges are per SOUND NAME, matching how patches store their sound (see soundsNote in seven-1.37.json). Never key them by sound id: ids differ between units.
keybed is an observation too. Nobody has counted this keyboard on the wire, and a keyboard drawn to the wrong length misplaces every fade on it.
low/high are positions in the drawing frame above, good for drawing a shape. They are NOT note-name evidence — `heard` is what was actually observed, and it is what the UI shows.
keybedNote: Reported by Daniel at the instrument (2026-08-12): the lowest key is an E, the highest key is an E, five full octaves — 61 keys. The octave NUMBERS here are a drawing frame only (E2-E7 chosen arbitrarily); nobody has read an absolute note off this keyboard, so the UI prints no note names for these ranges and neither should anything else. The shape is measured; the names are not.

Reed Piano.heard: the lowest A on the keybed up to the highest C
Reed Piano.derivation: lowest A above the bottom E = 45; highest C below the top E = 96

Vibraphone.heard: the second C from the bottom up to the top C
Vibraphone.derivation: C's on an E-E board are 48, 60, 72, 84, 96 — second from the bottom is 60, top is 96

coverage: Daniel, 2026-08-12: these two are believed to be the only restricted sounds on this unit. Recorded as his judgement, not as a sweep — no sound-by-sound survey was run, and the sampled expansions in particular have not been played end to end. The UI is unaffected either way: a sound with no entry still draws nothing, so a restriction missed here shows up as an absent picture rather than a wrong one.
